context: Evaluates whether the agent correctly handles a Terraform repeatable HCL block (capabilities { ... }) that serializes as a list of 0-or-1 objects in plan JSON, rather than treating it as a bare object. This is the pattern behind a real production bug: object.get(capabilities, "drop", []) silently fails to match when capabilities is [] rather than {}, so the rule never fires and the check appears to work in tests that mock the wrong shape.

checklist.name: Deny when capabilities block is absent (empty list)
checklist.description: A deny rule triggers when a docker_container resource has `capabilities` equal to `[]` (the real plan-JSON shape for 'no capabilities block configured') — not just when the `capabilities` key is missing entirely from the mock input

checklist.name: Deny when drop does not include ALL
checklist.description: A deny rule triggers when `capabilities` is a non-empty list whose first element's `drop` array does not contain `"ALL"` (e.g. `[{"drop": ["CHOWN"]}]`)

checklist.name: Capabilities read as a list, not an object
checklist.description: The policy iterates or indexes `capabilities` as a list (e.g. `some c in object.get(container.change.after, "capabilities", [])` or equivalent), rather than calling `object.get(capabilities, "drop", ...)` directly on the field as if it were a bare object

checklist.name: Tests use the real list-shaped mock, not a bare-object mock
checklist.description: Test fixtures represent `capabilities` as a list (`[]` or `[{"drop": [...]}]`), matching real `terraform show -json` output for a repeatable block — not as `{"drop": [...]}` or `{}`
